name: OODS Foundry — Claude Desktop (stdio)
summary: Connect Claude Desktop to OODS Foundry; the client starts it with npx.

env.MCP_EXTRA_TOOLS: comma-separated on-demand tools to add to the default surface, for example a11y.scan
env.MCP_SCHEMA_STORE_ROOT: where saved schemas, composed versions and file-mode output are kept; default ~/.oods-foundry from npm, the extracted directory from the archive
env.OODS_NODE_PATH: absolute path of the Node binary the adapter should start the server with; default: the Node running the adapter
env.OODS_MCP_APPS_UI: 1 offers the design preview app to a client that did not negotiate the MCP Apps extension; default: unset, only clients that negotiated it
env.OODS_OBJECTS_DIR: folder your own objects are read from, after the ones OODS Foundry ships; default ~/.oods-foundry/objects from npm, unset from the archive
env.OODS_TRAITS_DIR: folder your own traits are read from, after the ones OODS Foundry ships; default ~/.oods-foundry/traits from npm, unset from the archive
env.OODS_BRANDS_DIR: folder your own brands are kept and built in, outside the runtime; default ~/.oods-foundry/brands from npm, unset from the archive

notes: The client runs npx -y @oods/foundry. The first start downloads the package and unpacks its runtime once into ~/.oods-foundry/runtime/; later starts reuse it.

The node and npx the client starts must be Node 22.0.0 or newer; if the client cannot find npx, put its full path (what which npx prints) in command and give the client an env PATH that includes the directory of node.
Default surface: 19 tools. MCP_TOOLSET=all adds the 1 on-demand tools (20 in all).

Sent the runtime archive instead of using npm: use command node with args ["/path/to/oods-foundry-runtime/packages/mcp-adapter/index.js"], where /path/to/oods-foundry-runtime is the absolute path you extracted oods-foundry-runtime.tar.gz into (install.md beside the archive).
Restart Claude Desktop after saving the file; the tools appear under the oods-foundry server.

Claude Desktop's documentation says it renders apps from a local server only with Developer Mode on, so design_preview could show the running app inside the conversation there; this has not been tried with OODS Foundry, and otherwise the result is text with links to the preview in the browser, served on 127.0.0.1.

Register oods-foundry directly, beside any other entry such as an MCP hub, not behind it: the preview app reaches the conversation only when the client talks to the server itself or a hub passes the MCP Apps extension, the tool's _meta.ui and resources/read through.
After a newer version installs, choose Reload MCP Configuration: by its documentation, Claude Desktop keeps the tool list and the preview app it fetched until then.
